headline: India's markets regulator says it will soon publish rules on how AI may be used in the stock market.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a regulator's announced plan for AI rules in a large market, first reported in our editions today (speech on 10 Oct 2026), but the rules are not yet published.
importance_line: What changed: India's regulator has promised AI rules for its securities markets with human oversight and kill switches, which matters first to investors and brokers, then to exchanges and firms that use AI, but the guidelines are not yet published, so the tiers, duties and penalties are unknown.
summary: ET CIO reports that Tuhin Kanta Pandey, chairman of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the market regulator, said on Saturday 10 Oct 2026 that guidelines on the responsible use of AI and machine learning in capital markets will be issued shortly. He said the framework will be tiered, with clear accountability, data controls, kill switches (ways to shut a system down) and human oversight, and will line up with a supervisory toolkit for AI from the International Organization of Securities Commissions.
notes: Speech date (Saturday 10 Oct 2026) inferred from 'on Saturday' and the 12 Oct article date; first report of it in our editions. The article's opening summary paragraph (tender offers, buybacks) is not supported by the news text and was left out.
